_meta._mapper_provenance: stated in intake with hedge; flagged needs-verification in prior review. Mapper does not affect contract structure (it is _meta context, not an enforced constraint).
_meta.fit_summary: Third axis. RCR kept space + added economy/stats (~70% fit). Top Gun removed space, ran on scripts + skill-checks (~45% fit). Rad Racer FAKES space via rendering: the gameplay contracts are nearly empty (3-lane dodge + timer) while the entire identity lives in a rendering illusion the 9 contracts have no field for. This is the case that forces gameplay and rendering to be SEPARATE layers.
contracts_inapplicable: world_graph_contract  -> no traversable space; degenerate linear stage chain kept only to show the break
boss_contract  -> FIRST game in the corpus with zero bosses; contract is entirely empty
room_tile_contract  -> no 2D rooms; layout is a 1D sequence of track segments, moved to track_segment_contract
extensions_beyond_spec: rendering_illusion_contract  (THE headline -- forced-perspective road engine, sprite-scaling illusion, parallax. The game's whole identity. Bridges directly to the pixel/MCP engine.)
track_segment_contract  (1D pre-authored track pieces; correct replacement for room_tile in a forward-scroll game)
resource_contract  (time -- depleting; THIRD confirmation that resource economy is a missing primitive)
difficulty_scaling_contract  (speed is a single scalar that simultaneously drives rendering, difficulty, and time pressure)

needs_rom_extraction: exact stage count and per-stage time budgets
exact lane-shift speed / top speed / accel curve
exact obstacle spawn density per stage
frame counts (player car states, AI car scaling steps)

open_measure_flags: stage count modeled as 4 + final stretch; confirm
lateral movement modeled as continuous lateral position (not strict 3-lane); intake says 'discrete lane steps' AND 'pseudo-subpixel' -- reconcile against ROM
whether AI cars and obstacles share one timing-disruptor system or two separate spawners is unconfirmed

input_contract.theme: high-speed forward routing under time pressure
input_contract.setting: linear highway (desert / coast / city / night stages)
input_contract._strain: core_ability_style is just 'don't hit things while going fast' -- the field expects movement/combat verbs and there essentially are none

interpretation_layer._movement_model_strain: STRAIN: enum was (grounded | aerial | hybrid). Lane-based / rail movement is neither. The player moves laterally within a forward-locked frame.
interpretation_layer._combat_model_strain: STRAIN: enum was (projectile | melee | hybrid). There is NO attack -- the entire combat model is dodging. The contract has no value for 'no offense'.
interpretation_layer._world_structure_strain: STRAIN: same spatial-enum failure as Top Gun, different shape. Top Gun was scripted events; Rad Racer is continuous scroll.
interpretation_layer._progression_style_strain: STRAIN: not ability/key/hybrid. Progression is survive-the-stage, difficulty rises by speed + density.

world_graph_contract._INAPPLICABLE: No traversable space. Degenerate linear stage chain kept ONLY to show the break -- these 'nodes' are sequential stages on a forward-scroll, not navigable locations. Real layout is track_segment_contract; real structure is just an ordered stage list.

ability_system_contract._INAPPLICABLE: Zero abilities. The player never gains a capability. Empty by design.

player_controller_contract._strain: THIRD different break of this contract. RCR needed stat-scaling; Top Gun needed pitch/throttle; Rad Racer needs a lane/rail model with NO jump and NO HP. The platformer-shaped movement block is wrong again. Pattern is now conclusive: this contract is a platformer dialect, not a universal one.

movement_DEPRECATED_FIELDS._note: vertical motion in Rad Racer is a rendering illusion (bridge segments + scaling), not a physics field

collision_response._note: NO health pool. Cost of a crash is time + speed, not HP. Survivability == remaining time margin.

player_controller_contract._health_note: intentionally null -- this game has no damage model, only time/speed penalties

enemy_system_contract._note: Loosest clean fit, but STRAIN: enemies have no health -- they are non-destroyable timing disruptors. 'health: null' across the board. The contract assumes things you defeat; nothing here can be defeated.

boss_contract._INAPPLICABLE: FIRST corpus entry with zero bosses. Rad Racer has no boss concept at all. This proves even a 'core' contract is genre-optional.

room_tile_contract._INAPPLICABLE: No 2D room layout. Layout is a 1D ordered sequence of track segments. Moved to track_segment_contract.

track_segment_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Correct replacement for room_tile in a forward-scroll game. Pre-authored 1D track pieces streamed under the player.

rendering_illusion_contract._extension: EXTENSION -- and the single most important finding of the whole corpus. Rad Racer's ENTIRE identity is a rendering illusion, and the 9 contracts have NO rendering layer. This contract belongs to / overlaps the pixel-MCP engine. The intake's own verdict: strip the perspective system and it stops being Rad Racer even with every sprite intact.

forced_perspective_road._critical: the road is NOT geometry -- it is a per-row projection trick

rendering_illusion_contract.speed_coupling: rendering rate is driven by player speed -- the rendering and the difficulty share one variable (see difficulty_scaling_contract)
rendering_illusion_contract._engine_link: this is where Rad Racer feeds the pixel/MCP rendering core, NOT the gameplay generator. Gameplay-side, the game is trivial; rendering-side, it is the whole product.

resource_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Time as a depleting resource. THIRD confirmation of the resource-layer gap (RCR money = accumulate; Top Gun fuel = deplete; Rad Racer time = deplete). Resource economy is a primitive, not a per-game patch.

difficulty_scaling_contract._extension: EXTENSION. Rad Racer's defining design quirk: ONE scalar (speed) simultaneously drives rendering rate, reaction-window compression, sprite-flicker risk, and time pressure. The 9 contracts have no place to declare a unified scalar.

checks: stage_completable: each stage's track length is clearable within its time budget at achievable speeds
reaction_feasible: at max stage speed, the reaction window for the densest obstacle cluster is non-empty (i.e. physically dodgeable)
sprite_budget: peak simultaneous on-screen objects (cars + markers + scenery) respects the 8-per-scanline limit or schedules flicker (overlaps rendering/pixel MCP)
perspective_valid: row-compression curve converges to a single vanishing point (rendering correctness)
validation_layer._strain: Every spatial check (reachability, dead-ends, gate-solvability) is inapplicable AGAIN. Two of the four meaningful checks here (sprite_budget, perspective_valid) are RENDERING checks -- they belong to the pixel MCP, not the gameplay validator. This is the first game where the validator must span both engines.
